recentItems.title: Why you should date the short guy | Amy Chan | TEDxVancouver
recentItems.description:
As a leading relationship expert, Amy Chan reveals how our modern dating filters have triggered a "relationship recession." Discover the three hidden forces sabotaging your dating life and how to reprogram your brain for true connection. As a leading relationship expert, Amy Chan reveals how our modern dating filters have triggered a "relationship recession." Discover the three hidden forces sabotaging your dating life and how to reprogram your brain for true connection.

Amy Chan has been a trusted voice in modern relationships for nearly two decades, evolving from a dating columnist into a prominent authority on modern love and relationships.
In 2017, she launched Renew Breakup Bootcamp, a retreat blending psychology and neuroscience to help people heal from heartbreak. She also leads The Dating Bootcamp and is faculty at Esalen and the Omega Institute, where she teaches skills for building healthy, lasting relationships.

She is the author of the best-selling book Breakup Bootcamp: The Science of Rewiring Your Heart, which was featured in The New York Times and optioned by a major streaming network. Her latest book, UNSINGLE: How to Date Smarter and Create Love That Lasts, was published in April 2026.

recentItems.title: The momentum trap—and how to avoid it | Colleen Pimentel | TEDxMcMasterU
recentItems.description:
Colleen Pimentel challenges the idea that moving faster always means making progress. Her talk introduces the power of a “Strategic Pause,” encouraging audiences to step back, gain clarity, and ensure that the momentum we build is moving us in the right direction. Meet Colleen Pimentel, a Founder, Author, and GTM Business Leader with three decades of experience at tech giants like Google and Oracle. She is a leading advocate for "The Great Unlearning"—the process of trading external expectations for an authentic life defined by purpose rather than just achievement. This mission led her to a niche in transformational leadership, helping high-achievers navigate the "Fog" to reclaim their agency and fulfillment.

Throughout her 30-year career, Colleen mastered the art of reinvention, navigating over ten pivots while mentoring others to unlock their most purposeful professional chapters. Her battle-tested resilience inspired her book, Second Act, where she rewrites the rules of power and fulfillment for successful women. Colleen continues to advocate for psychological safety and authentic agency, with a goal of building corporate cultures and personal lives where individual voices are heard and truest powers finally step forward. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Running towards a life I love | Teesha Roy | TEDxWarwick Salon
recentItems.description:
Teesha shares her personal journey of living with ADHD and how taking up long-distance running helped her channel restless energy into clarity and discipline. She emphasizes breaking big goals into small steps, letting go of perfectionism, and finding strength in showing up authentically. Teesha, studying Data Diagnostics and Digital Health, is a passionate advocate for resilience, self-acceptance, and personal growth, using her journey with ADHD and running to inspire others.
Through fitness, she has redefined discipline and perseverance, proving that progress is built one step at a time. By embracing movement as a tool for clarity and confidence, she challenges the idea of perfection and encourages people to show up for themselves, despite obstacles. Her story is a testament to the power of authenticity, small consistent actions, and the courage to step outside societal expectations to create a path of one's own. recentItems.title: When Showing Up Is the Progress | Sahith Rajkumar | TEDxMcMasterU
recentItems.description:
Sahith Rajkumar challenges traditional ideas of progress by exploring the impact of consistently showing up for others. Drawing on his experiences in community outreach, he discusses how meaningful impact is not always defined by rapid or visible change, but by the commitment to stay engaged, especially when progress is uncertain. Sahith Rajkumar is an Honours Biochemistry student at McMaster University, researcher, and community advocate who challenges how we define progress. Through his work with Gore Park Community Outreach and Smiling Pillars, an initiative he founded to foster resilience and intergenerational connection, Sahith has spent over four years showing up consistently for communities in Hamilton.

His research in Indigenous health and HIV equity, combined with his sustained community work, has led him to question the metrics we use to measure impact. While progress is often celebrated as fast, visible, and upward, Sahith invites us to recognize another kind of momentum: the quiet strength of returning, rebuilding, and remaining present under constraint. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Rising Transport Fares: Fleeced or Milking The System? | Ruihan Ryan Shen | TEDxShahe Street Studio
recentItems.description:
What does a rising subway fare tell us about fairness, justice, and systems we take for granted? 
Ryan takes us on a philosophical adventure through the economics of metro systems, contrasting government-subsidized networks like Shanghai Metro with profit-driven models, like Hong Kong’s MTR. 
This talk ultimately concerns the balance of justice between the common good and market efficiency, asking us to reflect on whether everyday services should prioritize accessibility or self-sufficiency—and what that says about the kind of world we want to live in. Youth Public Affairs Observer

recentItems.title: 从沉默到看见：为什么我们要拍彼此的后脑勺？ | 子榆 司徒 | TEDxNanshan Salon
recentItems.description:
我们看不见自己的后脑勺，就像生活中，我们常常忽略那些“看不见”的事：家人隐藏的关爱，外卖骑手的辛劳，邻里擦肩而过的孤独。
现代社会以极致的高效和便捷掩盖了真实生活的粗糙：我们愈发习惯看结果，却遗忘了过程中的情感、牵挂与付出。
青年作家司徒子榆，从生活细节出发，通过家人的默契与陌生人的互动提醒我们：学会“看见”生活里不曾被注视的背面，也是在让这个世界多一分深爱和真实。 青年诗人、作家
跨媒介文化实践者 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: ٣٠ رصاصة لحماية حياتك المهنية | Ebrahem Anwar | TEDxYouth@TabaryElHegazHS
recentItems.description:
كم يمكن أن تكلّفك غلطة واحدة في عالم الأعمال؟

قد تكون الفكرة رائعة، والحماس في أعلى مستوياته، والطموح بلا حدود… ومع ذلك، قد تخسر سنوات من العمل بسبب قرار واحد لم تستعد له جيدًا.

في هذا الحديث، يشارك إبراهيم أنور خلاصة رحلة امتدت لأكثر من 15 عامًا في عالم الأعمال، والاستشارات والعمل مع أكثر من 100 شركة، مستعرضًا مجموعة من الدروس التي تحولت مع الوقت إلى ما يصفه بـ «30 رصاصة لحماية حياتك المهنية».

من معرفة نقاط قوتك واختيار الفريق المناسب، إلى أهمية توثيق الاتفاقات، وبناء رؤية واضحة، وإدارة المال، والتميّز عن المنافسين، والتفاوض، والتعامل مع الفشل، وبناء العلاقات، وصولًا إلى الحفاظ على نفسك من الاحتراق المهني.

كل «رصاصة» في هذا الحديث وُلدت من تجربة حقيقية؛ من خسارة، أو خطأ، أو قرار، أو درس لم يكن من السهل تعلّمه.

ففي عالم الأعمال، لا يكفي أن تعرف كيف تنجح…
بل تحتاج أيضًا إلى أن تعرف كيف تحمي نفسك من الأخطاء التي قد تمنعك من الوصول.

هذا الحديث ليس وصفة للنجاح، بل مجموعة من الدروس التي كان يتمنى إبراهيم أن يعرفها قبل أن يبدأ.

فإذا كنت في بداية طريقك المهني، أو تبني مشروعك، أو تبحث عن طريق أكثر وعيًا في عالم الأعمال… فالسؤال ليس: كيف تنجح فقط؟

بل: ما الرصاصة التي ستبدأ بها؟

recentItems.title: 用镜头夺回叙事权：谁来决定，我们的人生里什么值得被看见？ | 洁云 翁 | TEDxNanshan Salon
recentItems.description:
在主流叙事中，麻风病康复者常被标签化为可怕的传染者、需要救助的弱者，或是苦难的化身。但如果我们的镜头只聚焦于他们的伤痛，就真的看见了他们的人生吗？
何纪文，这位麻风病康复者，用一台普通的数码相机讲述了另一种人生。他的镜头定格的不只是苦难，而是村庄的风景、村民之间温暖的合作，甚至是阳光下盛开的桃花与歌声。从“被记录的对象”到“自己的叙述者”，他用行动夺回了叙事的权利，证明每个人都能决定，什么才是生命中真正值得被看见的部分。
本场演讲中，康复村志愿者翁洁云探讨了一个深刻的问题：当我们只以同情和标签看待受苦者时，是否无意间剥夺了他们作为一个完整“人”的权利？或许，重新看见他们，也是在重新审视我们自己。 JIA工作营康复村对话项目负责人
中央民族大学人类学硕士 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: カッコいい自分を妄想して、前進するパワーに | Atsushi KURASAKO | TEDxKumamoto
recentItems.description:
倉迫 諄 :  カッコいい自分を妄想して、前進するパワーに

大分県内のTOP高校に通う倉迫は、高校3年生の夏に、イタリアへ留学した。
本来であれば受験生である時期に、なぜ、彼は留学を決意したのか。
そういった難しい決断をする時の指針として、彼はいつも「妄想」をしている。
妄想が前に進んでいくパワーになっていることを、体験を通して語る。


KURASAKO Atsushi : Visualizing the "Cool Me": Turning Imagination into the Power to Move Forward


While most high school seniors in Japan were buried in textbooks, Kurasako, a student at a top school in Oita, chose a different path: Italy. 
Why did he decide to study abroad during the most critical year of his academic journey? 
The secret lies in his unique guiding principle — "visualizing the cool Me" In this video, he shares how the power of imagination can become the ultimate fuel for taking bold steps in life.


 He has accumulated diverse experiences such as classical ballet, musical theater, piano, track and field, and literary club activities for years. He has been learning vocal music since he was 8 and came in third in the national competition.

He sang the national anthems alone in public at the Oita Prefecture Koshien preliminary match.

Last year, he studied abroad in Italy as a Rotary Youth Exchange Student.

He continues to work hard daily to become a singer. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Knowing Precedes Doing: Creative Experiments in Leadership | L.V. Navaneeth | TEDxBITSHyderabad
recentItems.description: L.V. Navneeth, CEO of The Hindu Group, shares his leadership philosophy that "knowing precedes doing". recentItems.title: Has AI Earned the Right to Act? | Hemang Upadhyay | TEDxWisdom World School Amanora
recentItems.description:
What happens when we give AI the power to make decisions, but forget to ask whether it should be making them in the first place?

As artificial intelligence moves beyond answering questions and begins recommending, approving and acting on our behalf, the conversation around AI needs to move beyond how intelligent it is. Hemang Upadhyay explores a more important question: has AI earned the right to act?

Drawing from over 16 years of experience in technology, digital products and AI, Hemang examines what happens when automated systems operate with incomplete information, unclear boundaries or no clear path to challenge their decisions. He argues that automating a bad decision does not fix it. It simply allows the decision to travel faster.

The talk presents five principles for building AI that deserves trust: evidence, authority, visibility, restraint and recovery. Together, they offer a practical way to think about responsible AI without treating innovation and human judgment as opposing forces.

As AI becomes part of everyday decisions involving money, work, education, health and opportunity, the next generation will need to understand not only how to build powerful technology, but also how to decide where that technology should stop.

AI can generate options. Humans must decide which options are worth choosing.

The future is not about humans versus machines. It is about building technology powerful enough to help us and responsible enough to know when human judgment must remain in control. Hemang Upadhyay is a strategic Product and AI leader with over 16 years of experience transforming complex ideas into scalable products, digital platforms, and meaningful customer experiences. His work spans enterprise AI, digital commerce, customer experience, product data, and business transformation.

An industry speaker, published author, advisor, mentor, and judge for global technology and innovation programs, Hemang helps organizations move beyond AI experimentation toward responsible and measurable implementation. He is passionate about helping people overcome the fear of change, develop an adaptive leadership mindset, and recognize technology as a tool to expand human potential rather than replace it. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What Poetry Can Teach Us About Life | Vijay S | TEDxWisdom World School Amanora
recentItems.description:
What if some of life's most useful lessons are already hidden in just a few lines of poetry?

In a world filled with self-help books, step-by-step frameworks and endless advice on how to live better, Vijay Sharma takes us somewhere much simpler: Urdu shayari and poetry.

Through timeless verses and the wisdom of poets, this talk explores how a few carefully chosen words can help us understand happiness, pain, desire, uncertainty and the challenges we experience in everyday life. Sometimes, we don't need another framework or another list of things to fix. Sometimes, we simply need words that help us pause, acknowledge what we are feeling and see it differently.

Vijay draws attention to the enduring power of poetry as a form of wisdom that does not require a subscription, an update or a step-by-step manual. A couple of lines can stay with us, travel with us and offer perspective whenever we need it.

As the next generation grows up surrounded by increasingly complex information and instant solutions, perhaps there is something valuable in returning to an older form of wisdom—one that asks us not always to solve what we feel, but sometimes to simply understand it.

Because sometimes, the right two lines can teach us what an entire book tries to say. Vijay is a technology professional, entrepreneur and avid admirer of Urdu poetry and shayari. He has a deep appreciation for the timeless wisdom, emotions and simplicity found in poetry, and enjoys exploring how a few carefully chosen words can offer perspective on life, its challenges and the moments we often struggle to express. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
